why.net/grug/minecraft/forge/ForgeAdapter: getGameDirectory is read while the game boots, and the coverage map leaves the boot segment out, so no test shows it; miningCrackForTest draws the crack overlay only a client has.
why.net/grug/minecraft/forge125/Grug125Adapt: The game directory, which the boot and the client's resource reads ask for. The map leaves the boot segment out, and a dedicated server reads no resources.
why.net/grug/minecraft/forge125/Grug125Clien: The client half of the 1.2.5 loader: the mining crack overlay and the screen only a client opens.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugModFileState: Hot reload swaps a changed file aside on the client's watcher; a dedicated server reloads no mod file.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugModels: Reads a mod's model files, which a client does to draw a block or an item; a dedicated server draws nothing and reads none of them.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugModsWatcher: The reload count Test.reload_count reads after the client's watcher reloaded a file; a dedicated server reloads no mod file.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugQuad: Rotates model geometry while a model is built for drawing; a dedicated server builds none.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugScreenshots: Compares a captured frame with its reference; a dedicated server draws no frame to capture.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/GrugScreenshots$: The result of a GrugScreenshots comparison, which only a client's captured frame produces.
why.net/grug/minecraft/grug/HostFunctions: Reached only by tests that open a menu or read a frame: GUI.add_crafting_result serves a slot a menu draws, Test.mining_crack reads the client's crack overlay, Test.reload_count reads the client's hot reload, and Screenshot.equals compares a captured frame. A test that runs on a dedicated server does none of that today; #1040 gives every test a server run.
why.net/grug/minecraft/ornithe/OrnitheAdapte: The game directory, which the boot asks for and the coverage map leaves out of the boot segment; no test calls it.
why.net/grug/minecraft/stationapi/StationApi: The game directory the boot asks for, which the map leaves out of the boot segment, and the packet that carries a GUI to the client which opened it.
why.net/grug/minecraft/stationapi/resource/G: Registers the mods' resources as a resource pack, which only a client's pack list asks for; a dedicated server serves no resources.
